subject: Prettying up plots: axis text, legend, colours, aligning

messages.author: 4024e1d3d6b890f6
messages.subject: Prettying up plots: axis text, legend, colours, aligning
parts:
I'm new to R and ggplot2 and have a few questions regarding prettying up plots. I've produced some output from my data, mostly by trying things I've seen on this group and other places, and have almost what I'd like.

I've attached example source and data files and a pdf generated by a more complete version of the source.

Some of the things I'm having trouble with are:

1. Reformatting the y-axis scale text on the first plot: I'd like to display multiples of millions as 0, 5M, 10M, 15M, preferably with no M on the zero tick mark, and preferably changing automatically as I alter the scale.

2. Selecting colours for the points and lines on the plots. While the first plot's colours have come out by complete accident conveniently different and contrasting (it also looks better with more complete data, where Input is generally an order of magnitude greater than Matched), the second hasn't. How do I a) generate the moving average line in the second plot in a different colour to the points, b) select colours for the points and lines in the first plot or c) at least keep the colours the same for similar objects in both plots?

3. How can I change the title of the legend and the text for a legend element? e.g change "Type" to "Legend" and change "mavgInput" to "Moving avg of Input"? Can I break that text over two or N lines?

4. Can I use ggExtra::align.plots to align the time scales of both plots? i.e. the legend will "stick out" to the right of both plots. I haven't tried this at all yet, but from some reading on this group it seems I might have to use a patched version and also remove the plot titles, which I'd prefer not to do.

5. Alternative to #4: can I at least position the legend on the bottom of the first plot and have all legend items print out horizontally instead of vertically? i.e. Legend title and items all on one line.

Thanks in advance for any help.

regards - David

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Prettying up plots: axis text, legend, colours, aligning
parts: > 1. Reformatting the y-axis scale text on the first plot: I'd like to display multiples of millions as 0, 5M, 10M, 15M, preferably with no M on the zero tick mark, and preferably changing automatically as I alter the scale.

See the breaks and scales argument to scale_y_continuous. It's not
possible to do this in a completely automated way yet.

> 2. Selecting colours for the points and lines on the plots. While the first plot's colours have come out by complete accident conveniently different and contrasting (it also looks better with more complete data, where Input is generally an order of magnitude greater than Matched), the second hasn't. How do I a) generate the moving average line in the second plot in a different colour to the points, b) select colours for the points and lines in the first plot or c) at least keep the colours the same for similar objects in both plots?

Either use scale_colour_manual to exercise complete control, or set
the limits on scale_colour_discrete to ensure consistency across
plots.

> 3. How can I change the title of the legend and the text for a legend element? e.g change "Type" to "Legend" and change "mavgInput" to "Moving avg of Input"? Can I break that text over two or N lines?

opts(title = "My title")
labs(colour = "Colour legend title\nsecond line")

> 4. Can I use ggExtra::align.plots to align the time scales of both plots? i.e. the legend will "stick out" to the right of both plots. I haven't tried this at all yet, but from some reading on this group it seems I might have to use a patched version and also remove the plot titles, which I'd prefer not to do.
You'll have to ask Baptiste about that.

> 5. Alternative to #4: can I at least position the legend on the bottom of the first plot and have all legend items print out horizontally instead of vertically? i.e. Legend title and items all on one line.

Not yet, but soon, I hope.

Hadley

parts:
Sorry, Baptiste, to be clearer:

With the version of ggextra I have (2.11.1), this code sequence works and aligns the plots:
    # define the two viewports for plotting the charts in a grid
    pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(PLOT_ROWS, PLOT_COLS)));

    # plot the volume chart in its viewport
    print(volPlot, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = VOL_PLOT_ROW,
                                 layout.pos.col = VOL_PLOT_COL));

    # plot the error rate chart in its viewport
    print(pctPlot, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = PCT_PLOT_ROW,
                               layout.pos.col = PCT_PLOT_COL));

    # align the plots <= this aligns the plots
